title: London System: the pyramid, the preserved bishop, and Ne5

difficulty.label: London player who wants the setup to be decisions, not habit

objective.summary: You chose the London and Black challenged the centre at once. Build the pyramid in its proven order — e3, Nbd2, c3 — answer ...Bd6 by preserving the bishop on g3, and land the knight on e5 with the position already telling you why: after ...Nxe5 dxe5, the pawn attacks d6 and f6 at the same time.

planClasses.label: Build c3/d4/e3 in the order that answers ...Qb6
planClasses.description: The pyramid's construction order is the London's real theory: e3 before c3 keeps the queen's defence of b2 intact one move longer, and Nbd2 arrives before ...Qb6 can make Rb1 necessary. Position-specific counting, not general doctrine.

planClasses.label: Preserve the dark bishop, then attack with Ne5 and f4
planClasses.description: The bishop left home before e3 was played — the whole point of the system. When ...Bd6 offers the trade, Bg3 declines it; when ...Nxe5 removes the knight, dxe5 turns the outpost into a fork; and f4 behind the e5 pawn is the attacking plan the pyramid was built to launch.

planClasses.label: Know your recaptures before the tension resolves
planClasses.description: Two standing rules the spine drills implicitly: ...cxd4 is met by exd4 (keeping c3 as d4's guard and opening the e-file side of the pyramid), and ...Bxg3 is met by hxg3 (a machine-checked capture that opens the h-file toward Black's short-castled king).

annotations: The second stone of the pyramid, laid only after the bishop is out. Note the order: e3 before c3, so the d1 queen still watches b2 when ...Qb6 ideas appear.
The knight takes its London square: it guards the e4/c4 entry points, supports a later Ne5 recapture, and deliberately leaves c3 free for the pawn.
Black builds the mirror pyramid — and locks the c8 bishop behind it. Your bishop is outside its chain; theirs is not. That asymmetry is the London's entire positional claim.
The pyramid is complete: c3 guards d4, d4 leans on e5, and every recapture is scripted before it happens.
The standard challenge: Black offers to trade the piece your system is named after.
Decline it. On g3 the bishop keeps the b8-h2 diagonal, and if Black ever takes it, hxg3 opens the h-file toward the king that is about to castle short.
The light bishop takes the diagonal that points at h7 — the second barrel of the coming kingside plan. Your decision point is next: what is the follow-up worth building toward?
Black prepares ...Bb7, finally giving the locked bishop a diagonal. One move of freedom for them is one free move for you — spend it on the outpost.

The London's signature move, played with its arithmetic visible: if ...Nxe5 then dxe5, and the e5 pawn attacks both the d6 bishop and the f6 knight — a machine-checked fork geometry. If Black declines, f4 arrives behind the knight and the kingside plan begins.

checkpoints.label: ...Bd6 met by Bg3 — the system's piece survives
8.Bd3 — choose what the pyramid is for
Ne5 — the fork geometry stands behind the knight
You are past the authored line

deviations.note: 5.dxc5 cashes the centre for a pawn Black usually regains: the walked line ...e6 shows the simplest recovery route, and the pyramid the system is named for never gets built. Whether the pawn can be kept is unverified — play it and find out what you give up trying.

6.c4 breaks the London contract mid-build and steers for Queen's Gambit structures with the bishop already outside. A legitimate hybrid with its own theory; inside this pack it is a different opening wearing your move order.

7.Bxd6 Qxd6 concedes the trade to gain time and simplicity: the walked recapture leaves Black's queen developed but the dark-square bishop pair question closed. A sound, drier choice — the pack's spine keeps the bishop because the pack's claim is about what the bishop is for.

feedbackClaims.text: At the 1400/1600/1800 rating bands (Lichess blitz+rapid, 2024-01 through 2026-07), the London position after 3.Bf4 was reached 3,851,145 times and White scores 50.4% against 44.5% — one of the strongest White results among the family roots measured in this repo's priority artifact.
Ne5 carries its own tactical justification: after ...Nxe5 dxe5, the e5 pawn attacks d6 and f6 simultaneously — derived square arithmetic on the machine-walked line, true regardless of evaluation.

A system opening's theory is its construction order: bishop out before e3, e3 before c3, Nbd2 before ...Qb6 matters — the London fails at club level mostly when the stones are laid in the wrong sequence, not when Black plays a refutation.

RATING-BAND FREQUENCY (mechanical): content/candidates/priority/priority.json, Lichess explorer at ratings 1400/1600/1800, blitz+rapid, 2024-01 through 2026-07. Used here: the D02 row — 3,851,145 games, whitePct 50.4 / drawPct 5.1 / blackPct 44.5. No deeper-node frequency was retrieved; note the row's top Black reply is 3...e6 (28.1%) while this spine drills the 3...c5 challenge (11.7%) because that is the CC0 mainline row.

SPINE TRUNK: emitted by the openings sourcing pipeline (content/candidates/d02-queen-s-pawn-game-london-system, learner-side white, split-ply 6; the candidate directory is shared with the mirrored Black pack and records the most recent emit's job arguments). Hand-added plies 12-17 (...Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3 b6 Ne5) and all three deviations were walked move-by-move with a chessops scratch harness this session. The Ne5 fork claim (after ...Nxe5 dxe5 the pawn attacks d6 and f6) and the hxg3 h-file fact are derived square arithmetic on walked positions; the harness also refuted an earlier draft claim (...Bxg3 is illegal after dxe5 — the e5 pawn blocks the diagonal), which is why the annotations state geometry and not combinations.

UNGROUNDED: every strategic claim — the objective summary, the plan-class descriptions, all spine annotations, all deviation classifications and notes, and the non-derived feedbackClaims — is agent-authored prose with NO citation, NO engine evaluation and NO human review.
graduationBlockers: There is no pack review workflow in this system and there never will be one (owner ruling 2026-08-13). Only a citable source or mechanical validation that bears on the claim clears a blocker.

This pack has NO shapes reference, deliberately: no library entry names the London wedge (c3/d4/e3 with the dark bishop outside) — bishop-good-bad is an endgame entry with different plan ownership, and closed-centre-chain's trigger is French-pinned. A London/system-pyramid shape entry is the commissioned ask, mirroring the wave-3 dxc5-residue precedent.
The 'order is the theory' claim — that Londons fail by construction order rather than refutation at these bands — is a measurable corpus hypothesis nobody has measured.
The spine drills the 3...c5 row while 3...e6 is the more common reply at band (28.1% vs 11.7%); a companion line for the ...e6/...Bd6 move orders is unwritten.
No engine validation pass has been run on any position in this pack.
